issues.body: assemble_competitors() checks only isinstance(entry.get("id"), str), so {"competitors":[{"id":""}]} is accepted by --check and merged into the assembled registry. An empty ID is not a usable stable identifier for the downstream ID-based gather path, making the entry effectively unaddressable and defeating the same no-anonymous-record safety property now enforced for benchmark fragments. The existing test covers a missing ID but not an empty one.
issues.fix_hint: Require competitor IDs to be non-empty after applying the project's intended whitespace policy (at minimum, reject id == ""; preferably reject whitespace-only IDs too), and add focused regression cases for empty and whitespace-only string IDs in scripts/tests/test_bench_registry.py.
issues.title: Competitor fragments accept empty IDs

verdict.summary: The round-1 per-entry benchmark-ID defect is fixed and directly regression-tested, and the focused 31-test assembler suite passes. However, the parallel competitor-fragment validator still accepts an empty competitor ID. That violates the fragment registry's load-bearing identifiable-entry invariant and permits a competitor that normal ID-based gather selection cannot meaningfully address. Because this is a newly identified correctness gap, progress is regressing under the required comparison scale.
